evidence.note: CONFIRMED: bound_show clips long strings but keeps every gate evidence chunk_findings list entry and every triage finding, so items with 100+ review findings overflow the MCP surface budget. Measured on this repo: ddflow_show B-gap-lanes = 137047 chars (gates 73119 triage 55259), DX-lease-progress-breakable ~65KB. Capping the repeatable lists/triage to a fixed count is the fix.

Followed r-gemini-key-load (export GEMINI_API_KEY from [REDACTED:path] before review) and r-surface-budget (cap the MCP body with exact counts, point to ddflow --json show). Agreed with the existing mcp_bound convention: counts are exact, a cut says so, CLI --json is whole.

Added FINDINGS_SHOWN and _cap_findings to bound_show: every list inside a gate record and each gate triage is capped to 10 entries, counted in truncated.findings_cut, all -> ddflow --json show. Regression test test_show_caps_gate_findings_and_triage_and_counts_what_it_left_out fails before (AttributeError FINDINGS_SHOWN + unbounded) and passes after.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test does not verify the core promise that the **first** findings are kept. It only checks `len(...) == B.FINDINGS_SHOWN`, the cut count, and total JSON size. An implementation that keeps the **last** `B.FINDINGS_SHOWN` findings (or any arbitrary subset of that size) from `chunk_findings` and `triage["critic"]` would satisfy every assertion in this test while still dropping the first findings, contradicting the stated behavior. The test also uses only one gate, so “each gate’s triage” is asserted for only one gate; a broken implementation that caps triage only for the first gate would still pass.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test claims the bounded output “keep[s] the first findings”, but it constructs all 150 `chunk_findings` entries as identical `dict(finding)` copies and all 150 triage values as identical too. It then asserts only the surviving container length and the aggregate `findings_cut` count. An implementation that keeps the last `FINDINGS_SHOWN` entries, or any arbitrary sample, still preserves each length and the same `(150 - B.FINDINGS_SHOWN) * 2` count, remains under 20 KB, and includes the `--json show` pointer; for triage it also keeps the same number of keys, though not necessarily the first ones. The test is therefore vacuous for the central “first findings are kept, the rest are omitted” behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_payload_bound.py:test_show_caps_gate_findings_and_triage_and_counts_what_it_left_out

chunk_findings.detail: The ceiling is never enforced. `_cap_findings` only shortens lists longer than 10 and the top-level triage dict; `bound_show` then returns that tree with no check of `json.dumps` size. Given `{"state":"open","gates":{"critic":{"outcome":"passed","evidence":{f"k{i}": "x"*160 for i in range(200)}}}}`, every string is at `TEXT_SHOWN` so `_clip` leaves them whole, no list exceeds `FINDINGS_SHOWN`, `truncated` is omitted, and the result is still about 32 KB — over the 20 KB r-surface-budget the bug names. The same overflow happens with one kept finding whose body is a dict of ~200 long fields, or with ~30 gates each holding 10 clipped findings. The new test only builds one list of 150 small dicts plus one triage map, so it stays under 20 KB and does not fail on these inputs.

chunk_findings.detail: The capping code never modifies the caller’s `out`. `walk` builds new lists and dicts, and `out = walk(out)` only rebinds the local parameter; the function returns just `dropped[0]`. `bound_show` then calls `_cap_findings(out)` and `_shrink_to_budget(out)`, but its `out` remains uncapped. For the prior nested counterexample `{"state":"open","gates":{"critic":{"outcome":"passed","evidence":{f"g{i}": {f"k{j}": "x"*160 for j in range(10)} for i in range(40)}}}}}`, `json.dumps(out)` is still far above `SHOW_MAX_CHARS` and the 20 KB surface budget. `_shrink_to_budget` loops with the same oversized JSON and exits when `cap` reaches zero, leaving the returned body oversized while reporting a positive `findings_cut` from the unchanging original input. Previous HIGH items 1 and 3 therefore still hold.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:_cap_findings

chunk_findings.detail: The size loop is not a ceiling. It only re-slices lists and scalar leaf-maps, then exits when `cap` hits 0 even if `json.dumps(out)` is still over `SHOW_MAX_CHARS`. A gate evidence map whose values are dicts is never shortened, so its keys (and any mixed dict that also holds a nested dict) survive every pass. Given `{"state":"open","gates":{"g":{"evidence":{f"{'k'*80}{i}": {"child": {"only": 1}} for i in range(400)}}}}`, `_cap_findings` never slices the outer map, cap 0 only empties the inner `{"only": 1}` leaf-maps, and the serialised body stays well above 16_000 characters (roughly 400 keys of length 80 plus `{"child":{}}`). `bound_show` still returns that body, so B-show-mcp-result-over-ceiling is not closed for this shape. The new test only uses inner leaf-maps of strings, which this loop does shrink.

An implementation that kept the last 10 keys, or any arbitrary 10 keys, would still observe length 10, `findings_cut == 200 - FINDINGS_SHOWN`, and JSON `< 20_000`, so the test would pass while violating `_cap_findings`’s documented first-N behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_payload_bound.py:test_show_caps_a_leaf_map_the_string_clip_leaves_under_the_threshold

chunk_findings.detail: The new leaf-map cap only runs when every value is a non-dict, non-list scalar, so a series of finding records still is not capped and `bound_show` still has no `json.dumps` size check. Given `{"state":"open","gates":{"critic":{"outcome":"passed","evidence":{f"f{i}":{"detail":"x"*160} for i in range(200)}}}}`, the outer map fails the `all(not isinstance(v,(dict,list)))` test, each inner map has length 1, 160-character strings stay under the string clip, `truncated` is omitted, and the result is still about 32 KB, over the 20 KB budget. The same miss happens if one nested value is mixed into an otherwise scalar map of 200 `"x"*160` entries: that single nested value exempts the whole map.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:_cap_findings

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression only asserts `len(evidence)==FINDINGS_SHOWN`, `findings_cut==200-FINDINGS_SHOWN`, and size under 20 KB. Keys are distinct (`k0`..`k199`), but nothing checks which keys survive, so an implementation that keeps the last `FINDINGS_SHOWN` items (or any sample of that size) still passes while violating the “first FINDINGS_SHOWN” contract the sibling test now pins.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_payload_bound.py:test_show_caps_a_leaf_map_the_string_clip_leaves_under_the_threshold

chunk_findings.detail: The diff removes the `walk(out)` call, so `_cap_findings` no longer walks or caps anything except `out["triage"]`. For a `ddflow_show` body with no `triage` and a large `gates` map, e.g. `{"state":"open","gates":{f"g{i}":{"outcome":"passed","evidence":{"note":"x"*160}} for i in range(200)}}}`, no gate record or evidence map is visited, `findings_cut` is 0, and `_shrink_to_budget` calls the same `_cap_findings` and also does nothing. `bound_show` then returns a body whose `json.dumps` length is far over `SHOW_MAX_CHARS` with no `truncated` flag, so the over-ceiling bug remains unfixed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:_cap_findings

chunk_findings.detail: The new fallback cannot cap a nested dict-of-dicts, so it can exit with the body still over budget. Given `out={"triage":{"g":{"evidence":{f"f{i}":{"detail":"x"*160} for i in range(200)}}}}`, `walk` sees the 200-entry `evidence` map, but `all(not isinstance(v,(dict,list)))` is false for every one of its values, so `_cap_findings` drops nothing at caps 10, 5, 2, and 1; the `while` loop exits when `cap` reaches 0 with no final size check, and `bound_show` still returns an oversized body. This contradicts the new comment claiming `_shrink_to_budget` guarantees no nested shape slips past.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:_shrink_to_budget

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression only asserts serialized size <= `B.SHOW_MAX_CHARS` and a positive `findings_cut`. An implementation of `_shrink_to_budget` that simply deletes the entire `gates.critic.evidence` subtree (or drops all but one arbitrary inner entry) and reports `findings_cut = 400` satisfies both assertions: `json.dumps(out)` is tiny and `findings_cut > 0`. That passes the test while leaving `ddflow show` with no gate evidence or triage, contradicting the intended behavior. The sibling leaf-map test was tightened to verify the first `FINDINGS_SHOWN` keys survive; this new size-guard test has no corresponding check that any evidence is retained.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_payload_bound.py:test_show_stays_under_the_budget_for_a_nested_shape_the_caps_miss

chunk_findings.detail: The `_shrink_to_budget` function contains an infinite loop when `cap` reaches `0` and the serialised output still exceeds `SHOW_MAX_CHARS`. Given a deeply nested structure or large payload that cannot be reduced below `SHOW_MAX_CHARS` by integer division of `cap` (since `cap //= 2` will eventually hit `0` and stay `0`, causing `_cap_findings(out, 0)` to drop nothing), the `while len(json.dumps(out)) > SHOW_MAX_CHARS and cap > 0:` loop condition will never terminate once `cap` becomes `0`, hanging the entire process indefinitely when handling an oversized MCP result.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:_shrink_to_budget

chunk_findings.detail: The size loop only re-runs `_cap_findings`, which still refuses to shorten any dict whose values are dicts or lists, so a large `gates` map is never reduced and the loop exits over budget once `cap` hits 0. Given `body = {"state":"open","gates":{f"g{i}": {"outcome":"passed","evidence":{"note":"x"*160}} for i in range(200)}}`, every string is under the string clip, no list or scalar-leaf map exceeds the cap, `_shrink_to_budget` drops nothing, and `bound_show` still returns all 200 gates — on the order of 50 KB, past both `SHOW_MAX_CHARS` and the 20 KB surface budget. The same input from the earlier HIGH finding is unchanged by this delta.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:_shrink_to_budget

chunk_findings.detail: A map of finding records is also not a scalar leaf map, so halving the cap never touches it and there is still no fallback when `json.dumps` stays over `SHOW_MAX_CHARS`. Given `{"state":"open","gates":{"critic":{"outcome":"passed","evidence":{f"f{i}":{"detail":"x"*160} for i in range(200)}}}}`, the outer evidence map fails `all(not isinstance(v,(dict,list)))`, each inner map has length 1, strings stay under the clip, and after `_shrink_to_budget` the body is still ~40 KB with every `f0`..`f199` present. The new regression uses inner scalar maps (`{k_j: "x"*160}`), which `_cap_findings` does shrink, so it does not catch this shape.
